messages:
Priya Rao: Heads-up — escalated ticket from AcmeCorp. Their nightly indexer started failing after they switched to the new embedding model yesterday. Symptoms: 422 dim_mismatch when writing to their vector DB, and a bunch of 401s during backfill retries. Customer is seeing failed backfill + unexpectedly high token billing because retries keep re-hitting the embeddings endpoint.

Alex Chen: Seen the thread. Can you paste the exact error payloads and the model name they flipped to?

Priya Rao: Pasting logs from their upload job (sanitized):
```
ERROR 2026-03-14T22:01:03Z ingest: write failed: vectordb error: schema_mismatch: expected_dim=1024 actual_dim=1536
ERROR 2026-03-14T22:01:27Z embed-api: 401 unauthorized: invalid API key for org=acmecorp-service
WARN 2026-03-14T22:01:28Z backfill: retrying batch id=jb-20260314-42 attempt=3
```
They said they changed model in their config from `embed-lite-1024` -> `open-embed-1536-v2` around 21:45 UTC.

Marta Li: That explains dims. Vector DB schema locked at 1024 vectors; indexer rejects 1536. The 401s are probably due to credential rotation during the same window — we had a short key rotation job in the customer tenant that might have invalidated the old key.

ingest-bot: [alert] 1790123461 ingest.jobs.failed=38 severity=high tag=dim_mismatch org=acmecorp

Sean O'Neill: Quick repro steps we asked the customer to run:
1) curl to embeddings endpoint with a single doc and check vector length
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536-v2","input":"hello world"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```
They ran that and got `1536`.

Alex Chen: Ok. Root causes: (A) model swap produced 1536-dim vectors, (B) vectordb schema is strict at 1024, (C) retry storm + expired creds caused 401 spikes and extra billable calls.

Marta Li: Mitigation options:
- Short term: stop the backfill, throttle retries, and ask customer to revert model to `embed-lite-1024` if they need immediate indexing.
- Medium: support a conversion shim in the indexer that truncates or projects 1536->1024 (lossy) for backfill only.
- Long term: migrate vectordb schema to 1536 (requires reindexing existing vectors or storing separate index).

Priya Rao: Customer is on a committed Dedicated plan; they want minimal downtime. They asked for a quick fix so their search features don't break this afternoon. They are willing to pause new writes for a short window.

Alex Chen: Proposed immediate triage:
- Set `backfill.max_concurrent_jobs=1` for Acme tenant and `backfill.batch_size=16` (they were at 128).
- Add exponential backoff and cap retries to 3.
- Roll a temporary ingest shim in the pipeline that rejects 1536-sized vectors with a clear error so we don't waste token budget on repeated retries.

Marta Li: I can push the config flags for the tenant in config-service now. Will also add a metric to track `ingest.dim_mismatch.count`.

ops-bot: [note] 1790123490 billing.alert high_token_usage org=acmecorp estimation=$420 over expected

Sean O'Neill: For the auth 401s: we need TO validate if the customer's API key rotated or if our key validation service had a hiccup. Priya, can you confirm whether they did a key rotation?

Priya Rao: Confirmed with the customer: they rotated service keys at 21:50 UTC as part of routine policy. They didn't realize a backfill job was running. So the 401s line up.

Alex Chen: Action plan (short-term, 1–3 hrs):
- [Alex] Push tenant config: `backfill.max_concurrent_jobs=1, backfill.batch_size=16, backfill.retry_limit=3` — done in staging, will apply to prod for acme now.
- [Marta] Deploy ingest validation that returns a friendly 422 with `expected_dim=1024` when dimensions mismatch (prevents re-issuing embedding calls) — priority hotfix.
- [Priya] Ask customer to either revert to `embed-lite-1024` or pause backfill and reschedule once keys rotated.

Marta Li: I'll open a short-lived hotfix branch. Validation will be an inexpensive vector length check in the indexer before calling vectordb. Patch should be safe; risks: briefly rejecting legitimate mixed-dim datasets if they intended to migrate.

ingest-bot: [info] 1790123560 ingest.validation.patch=created branch=hotfix/dim-precheck author=marta

Priya Rao: Customer agreed to pause backfill and revert model for now. They want us to help create a migration plan to go to 1536 with minimal downtime.

Alex Chen: Migration options to propose:
- Option A: Side-index: create new 1536 index in parallel, populate with new vectors, then switch reads (fast but requires extra storage).
- Option B: Re-embed existing corpus with new model and backfill in phased windows (costly but consistent vectors).
- Option C: Add mixed-dim support in vectordb (store dim metadata and route queries to appropriate index) — engineering heavy.

Marta Li: I'll draft an internal migration proposal outlining costs, estimated time, and guidance. Priya, I'll cc the customer-facing doc.

Sean O'Neill: Postmortem items:
- Improve docs warning that model changes can change embedding dimension and break downstream schema.
- Add a preflight API that returns embedding config (dim, tokenization) for a model so customers can detect compatibility before flipping.
- Add tenant-level guardrails to prevent automated backfills running across credential rotations.

Priya Rao: Assigning follow-ups:
- Alex: confirm config changes applied and monitor rates (ETA 15m).
- Marta: cut hotfix PR for dim precheck and coordinate rollout (ETA 30–45m).
- Sean: draft postmortem template and preflight API proposal (ETA EOD).
- Priya: keep customer updated and coordinate migration options.

ops-bot: [reminder] 1790123600 run: monitor.ingest.dim_mismatch.count

Alex Chen: Config applied to Acme in prod. I'm seeing ingestion errors fall from ~120/min -> ~2/min (mostly old queued jobs). Billing spikes should plateau once retries stop.

Marta Li: Hotfix PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/hotfix/ingest-dim-check/pull/7. Rolling to canary in 2m.

ingest-bot: [info] 1790123625 canary.deploy=started shard=us-east-1 tag=hotfix-dimcheck

Priya Rao: Customer on the line is able to resume normal activity after reverting model. They're grateful for quick response. I'll keep them on a short call until the migration doc is ready.

Alex Chen: Leaving notes for follow-up telemetry: add `embed.model_dim` to trace spans so we can correlate model changes with downstream failures automatically.

Priya Rao: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until migration plan is delivered. Will update with customer decision. :thumbsup:
